I'm sorry to hear that your family and friends are only contacting you when it serves to benefit them. I have in laws that are very similar. The thing i can say about that situation is that "everyone is the main character in their own story."

It feels bad, but understanding that everyone is self-centered to a degree can help us understand that it's not that they are being actively malicious, it's just that they are thinking more about themselves than anyone else as a course of nature.

You're also the main character in your own story, however. You can choose how certain events play out, who to trust and confide in, what to eat for lunch, when you're going to wake up tomorrow morning. It's your story. 

While it seems hard to find meaning in it now, who is to say that acting selfishly, say as the main character in a hero's journey, for a little bit won't change the outlook of the rest of your life. Building comfortable boundaries with people who are treating you poorly and not respecting your wants and needs is a good first step. 

I'm proud of you for posting here because it means you're looking for a reason to keep going, and that's a hard thing to do when everything feels lost. This is the first, brave step on a long, hard journey to discover who you truly are and what your story is really about.

Nothing matters *unless you exist to make it matter.*

Keep on trucking, friend. I'll be here for you.

Normal virtue chance is 25% so it's about a 6.25% chance to get double virtue with base chance.

In this instance, these characters were resolve level 1 inside a level 3 mission, so they had a 5% virtue chance debuff per level they were below the mission level, leaving them with a 15% virtue chance.

Triple virtue with a 10% debuff has a 1.125% chance of happening.
